chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amraki ibn Ali, all together, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made Hajj obligatory upon those with the capacity (al-jiddah) every year,
and this is His word, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to Allah is the pilgrimage of the House for whoever is able to undertake a journey to it.'
And whoever disbeliees, then indeed Allah is Self-sufficient of the worlds.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So the one from us who did not perform Hajj, so he has disbelieved?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the one who says, 'It is not like this', so he has disbelieved'.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ هَذَا هَكَذَا: It is not like this (denial of obligation)

ai.seo_question: Does not performing Hajj make a Muslim a disbeliever?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between mere omission of Hajj and actual disbelief (kufr) by linking the obligation to the Quranic condition of ability (istita'ah). It establishes that denial of the obligation itself constitutes kufr, whereas failure to perform it due to inability or neglect does not, a key nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of those who delay the pilgrimage.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Musa Bin Al Qasim Al Bajaly, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, altogether, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Necessitated the Hajj upon the inhabitants of Al-Jiddah during every year,
and these are the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [3:97] and Pilgrimage to the House is incumbent upon the people for the Sake of Allah, (upon) every one who is able to undertake the journey to it;
and whoever disbelieves, then surely Allah is Self-sufficient, above any need of the worlds’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So the one from us who did not perform Hajj, so he has disbelieved?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but the one who says, ‘It is not like this’, so he has disbelieved’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajaliy and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali all from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother, , who has said the following:
“Abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam has said that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, made al- Hajj obligatory for people of Jaddah every year
because of His words, ‘It is obligatory upon people from Allah to perform al-Hajj who are able to do so.
Those who refuse must take notice that Allah is independent of all people.’

[3:96] I then asked him (the Imam); ‘Does one of us for not performing al- Hajj become an unbeliever?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘However, if he says, ‘This is not as such then he becomes one who hides the truth (an unbeliever).”’
